summary: Reproduce the reported reliability problems. Define one portable identity, command, context and selection contract.
description:
Purpose: Reproduce the reported reliability problems. Define one portable identity, command, context and selection contract.

Current state: this phase is planned; current production persistence remains JSON until the SQLite/API migration is implemented. Reuse existing capabilities instead of creating another planner.

Deliverables and sole owners:
- P116(F025)/T461: Reproducible baseline fixtures for the six reported failures and the new storage boundary.
- P116(F025)/T462: One domain contract for identity, eligibility, context, phase continuity and revision-aware results.

Execution contract:
Follow the task dependencies and the phase priority in the rebuilt F025 plan. Keep coherent phase work and recover approved detours; do not introduce a global task queue or silently preempt active work. Use the user-scoped service/SQLite boundary, explicit workspace identity, complete bounded context and revision-bound evidence wherever applicable.

Acceptance:
Each task proves its stated outcome; preserve IDs/history, single-owner decisions and phase handoffs. Mechanical parent/dependency effects are consistent; semantic review is factual, reviewed-unchanged or explicitly pending. Native/provider/installed claims need their actual owner evidence.

Supporting design: docs/agent-brain/architecture.md and docs/agent-brain/heca-protocol.md; current map .planner/docs/agent-brain-plan.md. This is one current phase contract, replacing the accumulated historical amendments. Do not migrate user data or perform Git/release actions merely because the plan is registered.

Child-contract reconciliation: The shared contract must define service-owned business rules before clients are converted; fixture behavior is not a production policy source.
goals: Define one portable identity, command, context and selection contract.
nonGoals: No unrelated runtime implementation, real data migration or Git/release action during planning.
No duplicate ownership, fixed language list or global task-queue scheduling.
risks: Old JSON/path assumptions can leak through direct consumers; inspect current integration seams.
A passing fixture or stored read does not prove live native behavior or model understanding.

tasks.title: Reproduce the reliability failures on isolated fixtures
tasks.description:
Outcome: Reproducible baseline fixtures for the six reported failures and the new storage boundary.

Current implementation: Handoffs, rules, claims, read tracking and recommendation already exist. Reports identify unreliable behavior; previous fixture reports do not certify this checkout.

Implementation responsibility:
- Build isolated old-format fixtures for several handoffs, repeated resume reads, ignored conventions, nested detours, current-phase priority bias and duplicate capability creation.
- Capture real core/MCP/Pi/server outputs and exact revisions, including same-task races, source workspace inference and failed/incomplete replies.
- Record bytes, characters, tool calls and model tokens where available; define comparable small/large-plan and no-op fixtures for later regression.
- Add the descriptor-missing/incompatible, missing-HOME and per-project-server assumptions to the migration baseline without changing real data.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Each reported case has a reproducible input and an observable expected correction; uncertain causes stay explicit.
- Fixtures use mkdtemp and stop owned processes; no real project is migrated or dashboard auto-started.
- Measurements distinguish product scenarios from synthetic SQL primitives.

**Completion summary:**
Shipped: reproducible baseline for the six reported reliability failures and the migration storage boundary, in four runnable suites (26 tests, all green) plus a checked-in measurement snapshot. Core (packages/plan-core/test/agent-brain-baseline.test.mjs, 16 tests): several handoffs surface as unranked competing claims with old-format phase-file read-back; repeated resume reads (fresh session needs task+phase+feature, unrelated writes stale persisted attestations); ignored conventions (unread guidelines never gate an eligible start; customized planner skill preserved, never reconciled); nested detours resolve LIFO one level at a time with standardized resume proposals; current-phase priority bias (currentPhaseId overrides global priority with no session-ownership check — AB-IMP-007; higher-priority empty phase silently skipped with no planning claim — AB-IMP-008); duplicate capability creation (managed skills idempotent, legacy copies adopted); same-task claim race between two PlanStore instances; failed/incomplete reply paths; migration boundary (descriptor missing = workspace undetectable, schemaVersion 999 rejected, legacy features.json migrates). MCP (packages/plan-mcp/test/agent-brain-baseline-mcp.test.mjs, 4 tests, real published server over stdio): same-task race between two sessions (one started=true, loser denied); readable failures for unknown task/phase and defined reply for incomplete args; source workspace inference captured live (AGENT_PLAN_ROOT unset -> cwd/.planner); scripted resume scenario measured at 6 tool calls, 1723 text bytes, 6699 structured bytes (~4x duplication) plus the REQUIREMENTS_READ_REQUIRED extra read per start. Server (packages/plan-server/test/agent-brain-baseline-server.test.mjs, 4 tests, real HTTP): per-project server isolation; same-task start race through POST /tasks/:id/start (one 200, one refusal 400, exactly one active owner); shaped failures for unknown entity and invalid write; missing-HOME evidence (empty HOME yields empty homedir() without throwing — user-scope installs must fail explicitly). Measurements (packages/plan-core/test/agent-brain-baseline-measurements.test.mjs + docs/agent-brain/baseline/measurements.json): no-op/small/large product scenarios (0/27/632 entities) — recommendation reply is size-bounded (1560 bytes at both 27 and 632 entities, claims capped at 8) while the full recommendation object grows (4566 -> 10341 bytes); model tokens recorded null as an explicit open boundary. Full narrative with expected corrections, uncertain causes and unverified boundaries: docs/agent-brain/baseline/README.md. Verification: all four suites green locally (26/26); no real project touched, mkdtemp isolation, owned processes stopped, no dashboard started. Exact revisions: feat/agent-brain @ 59f9028059e3b6206dd2545ec405f6fdc8d139e1, core/mcp/server 0.4.11. Remaining: none (Pi-adapter-level capture and model-token accounting stay model-visible, recorded as unverified boundaries).
tasks.notes: Appendix (2026-11-15, user-directed cleanup): after T461 completion, three stale full dev stacks (spawned by this session's multi-instance verification runs) plus one earlier orphan kept listening ports after their terminals were gone. All were stopped (9 processes + detached pnpm parents) and verified: zero listeners on 3090/5175-5178/60507/62526/62569. Root cause fixed structurally in scripts/dev-web.mjs (commit d574dd6, pushed): children are no longer spawned detached, so the whole chain shares one process group and receives terminal SIGHUP/SIGINT; explicit SIGHUP handler triggers clean shutdown; an orphan guard (process.ppid === 1, checked every 2s) shuts the stack down when the script is reparented to launchd. Empirically verified with three scenarios, each leaving zero survivors and free ports: SIGHUP to the process group (terminal-close emulation), direct parent death without group signals (orphan guard), and normal start/serve/SIGTERM operation (vite 200, api 200).

tasks.title: Define one shared next-work and context contract
tasks.description:
Outcome: One domain contract for identity, eligibility, context, phase continuity and revision-aware results.

Current implementation: Selection/read-order and adapter messages diverge. The accepted target is HOME SQLite behind a single application service, while current consumers still open JSON stores.

Implementation responsibility:
- Specify stable project/repository/workspace/caller/native-session/execution identities and the boundaries implemented by T489, the SQLite task and T490.
- Define owned active work and valid returns before globally ready feature -> phase -> task ordering. Preserve coherent phase work; no global task queue or automatic priority preemption.
- Define typed success/non-success, actual context delivery, retained-context restoration, role-aware API parity and source/target availability extension points.
- Map every baseline case to one implementation owner and define bounded mutation/resume/query/editor budgets with explicit continuation.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Core/MCP/Pi/server/UI can consume the same versioned result shapes.
- Dependency readiness is distinct from desired ordering and code/rationale relationships.
- Phase continuity does not add an unapproved global exclusive phase lock; the warning-only no-task guard remains.

**Completion summary:**
Shipped: one versioned shared domain contract at docs/agent-brain/domain-contract.md (contract v1, defined at feat/agent-brain @ d574dd6), linked from architecture.md status line and registered in the decisions.md Specifications table. Contents: (C1) the seven-identity contract — projectId, repository registration, workspaceId, planner caller, native harness session, executionId, actor/requester — each with meaning, stability, current carrier as dated evidence and implementing owner (T489 identity separation, T490 service/caller routing, T491 executions), plus five normative resolution rules (nearest descriptor wins, typed incompatibility, migration/initialization offers, no silent fallback — backed by the T461 baseline evidence for missing descriptor, schemaVersion 999 rejection and cwd inference); (C2) the seven-rule work-ordering ladder — typed conflict, owned active work, valid returns newest-first with LIFO checkpoints and other-session exclusions, global ready feature->phase->task by (priority, number), current-phase affinity restricted to ownership-checked reordering (recorded gap -> T509), empty-phase planning claim (AB-IMP-008 -> T510), on-hold ready-to-resume flags — plus the separate mandatory eligibility contract for explicit starts (startable statuses, parked-parent derivation exception, dependencies done except temporary overrides, once-worded refusals) with dependency readiness kept distinct from ordering; (C3) typed results and errors (bounded claim kinds/sources, standardized resume proposal, not-found vs ambiguous resolution, typed race refusals -> T496, shaped failures never crashing the host, apiVersion/fold-into-structured envelopes) and the full context-delivery contract (gated entities, sessionInfo attestation semantics with descriptionUpdatedAt as the phase/feature contract revision, Accepted-Decision completeness proof, delivery-not-understanding evidence, compaction restoration, bounded lossless chunking where overflow is never attested, role-aware parity); (C4) every T461 baseline case mapped to exactly one implementation owner in a table, and six bounded budgets with named constants verified against source (RECOMMENDATION_CLAIM_LIMIT=8, on-hold preview 160, decision/work-map 8000, project-context chunks 32000, RESUME_SESSION_LIMIT=20, start context block) each with an explicit continuation path; (C5) acceptance evidence — same-shapes-everywhere verified by source inspection (core functions consumed by plan-mcp and pi-adapter, plan-server rendering through the same builders), dependency-readiness/ordering separation verified in code, no-global-phase-lock and warning-only guard preserved per Accepted Decision 7995854e — with explicit unverified boundaries (no live multi-agent session evidence; SQLite service/descriptor/execution records not yet implemented; model comprehension and tokens unobservable). No implementation code was produced: this is the planning contract T489/T502/T490/T463+ implement.
tasks.notes:
Source-backed analysis (2026-11-15, checkout feat/agent-brain @ d574dd6) before writing the contract.

Current owning modules inspected (dated evidence, not permanent identity):
- packages/plan-core/src/task-selection.ts (503 lines): recommendNextTask is the pure harness-agnostic selector. Precedence ladder as implemented: session-owned active work (or typed 'conflict' when >1 active) -> live deviations newest-first (return-required states 'resume-required'/'resolved' treated identically, legacy synonym documented) -> other sessions' held resume tasks excluded -> most recent pauseSnapshot checkpoint (LIFO) -> currentPhaseId filter over globally ready planned tasks (overrides global priority UNCONDITIONALLY, no session-ownership check — the AB-IMP-007 baseline) -> global ready feature -> phase -> task by compare(priority, number). Claims bounded at RECOMMENDATION_CLAIM_LIMIT=8 with kind recommendation|advisory|conflict|insufficient and source priority|active-task|resume-deviation|dependency-ready|handoff|archived-handoff|on-hold. checkExplicitTaskStart keeps availability+dependency invariants mandatory while priority stays advisory (explicit starts never gated by priority). Empty higher-priority phases produce no planning claim (AB-IMP-008 baseline). buildResumeRequiredProposal is the standardized resume proposal shape.
- packages/plan-core/src/on-hold.ts (187): ON_HOLD_STATUSES=deferred/waiting/blocked; hold reason from the latest statusLog entry to the current status; refsNamedIn resolves F/P/T refs in prose (REF_IN_TEXT word-bounded); readyToResume = every named ref (reason refs + dependsOn edges, deduped by ref) finished; startedOpenPhaseIds scopes the list to phases already under way; renderOnHoldWork bounds preview at 160 chars, default limit 8.
- packages/plan-core/src/refs.ts (226): ref grammar UUID | shortId (5-char) | P00x / P00x(F00x) / F00x/P00x/T00x composites with parent validation | bare T00x globally unique | title fallback; resolveFeatureRefStrict distinguishes not-found from ambiguous with a typed error.
- packages/plan-core/src/read-tracking.ts (404): per-session read state (in-memory) + persisted sessionInfo attestations; storedReadState valid when entityRevision <= attestation.createdAt, stale when > ; entityRevision uses descriptionUpdatedAt for phase/feature when present (canonical contract revision), else updatedAt — this is the field an unrelated write must not bump (T461 baseline case 2); canonical full-read attestation (markCanonicalFullReadForSessionId) throws unless delivered content contains every field of every Accepted Decision; requiredReads report missing vs stale; projectGuidelinesReadStateForSession is currently advisory-only (read state never gates eligibility — AB-IMP-003 baseline).
- packages/plan-core/src/task-context.ts (239): bounded context builders — MAX_ACCEPTED_DECISION_CONTEXT_CHARS=8000, MAX_PHASE_WORK_MAP_CHARS=8000, truncateAtSafeBoundary with explicit truncation suffixes; buildPhaseWorkMap renders open work fully first, closed work one-line; buildPhaseContextBlock injects phase/feature/requirements/decisions/work-map into task_start replies (same reply for Pi and MCP).
- packages/plan-core/src/project-context.ts (383): PROJECT_CONTEXT_DELIVERY_VERSION=1, canonical snapshot + sha256 fingerprint + lossless chunking (DEFAULT 32000 chars) with ordered-cursor verification (verifyProjectContextChunks is the only producer of complete evidence); fingerprint-based read state missing/valid/stale; non-blocking stale advisory for planner-load refresh; buildProjectContextLoadReply folds text into structured (MCP host contract).
- packages/plan-core/src/session-focus.ts (47): taskOwnershipConflict, deviationsForSession (own + unowned only), RESUME_SESSION_LIMIT=20; a caller with no session id sees the whole project.
- packages/plan-core/src/schema.ts: TaskStatusSchema = planned|in-progress|done|blocked|canceled|rejected|deferred|waiting; WorkDeviationSchema states approved|active|resume-required|resolved|resumed|canceled with temporaryTaskId/resumeTaskId/ownerSession; Task.pauseSnapshot (nullable) and Task.activeOwnerSession are the atomic-ownership and checkpoint fields.

Precedents and relevance: architecture.md sections 3 (identities), 5 (command envelope, requestId idempotency, expectedRevision), 7 (context_reads record, delivery-not-understanding), 8 (execution lock in-progress/parked/abandoned with heartbeat lease, detour persistence A->B->C) already define the target boundary this contract must specify precisely; decisions.md fixes service/storage/identity and keeps 'no global individual-task queue' and the warning-only no-task guard. The T461 baseline (docs/agent-brain/baseline/README.md, 26 green fixtures) supplies the six failure behaviors this contract must subsume with explicit owner mapping. Existing bounded-budget constants (8 claims, 160-char reason preview, 8000-char decision/work-map, 32000-char project-context chunks) are the measured precedent for the contract's budget table.

Reuse and ownership: no new module or data flow is created by this task — it is a documentation contract that names the existing functions/constants as the current reference behavior and assigns each baseline case to its already-registered implementation owner (T463 selector unification, T464 nested returns, T465/T466 resume/context, T467-T469 conventions/skills, T489/T502/T490 storage/identity/service, T496 consistency, T509/T510 session-continuity and empty-phase claims). Conventions followed: decisions.md Specifications table gains one row; architecture.md links the contract; all text English; no Git publication beyond the user-approved commit flow.

Verification intent (checklist C5): link/consistency validation of the doc family (no dangling links, no contradiction with architecture.md/decisions.md), every baseline case traceable to one owner task, every budget traceable to a named constant in source, plus recording which boundaries stay unverified (no live multi-agent session evidence, no SQLite runtime yet).
